module.purpose: Manages font discovery, loading, caching, tracking, and CSS embedding for editor shapes and documents.
module.summary: This module provides the editor's font lifecycle boundary. It derives font faces from shapes through reactive caches, deduplicates FontFace instances per document, loads required fonts asynchronously, batches requests through microtasks and transactions, and converts font sources into embedded CSS declarations. Disposal invalidates manager caches while protecting against stale asynchronous load callbacks.
module.businessContext: Supports text rendering and document export in the editor. Failures can leave text incorrectly rendered, fonts duplicated, or exported CSS unable to reproduce typography.

detail.name: FontManager
detail.summary: FontManager coordinates discovery, caching, loading, and CSS embedding of fonts required by editor shapes. It reuses document FontFace instances and tracks asynchronous load state per font.

detail.signature: constructor(private readonly editor: Editor, private readonly assetUrls?: { [key: string]: string | undefined })
preconditions: editor is a valid Editor instance with a store that provides createComputedCache and createCache.
postconditions: The manager retains the supplied editor and optional asset URL mapping.
A computed cache for shape font faces is created.
A cache for per-shape font load state is created.
invariants: Shape font-face cache results are compared with areArraysShallowEqual.
Shape records used by the computed cache are compared with areShapesContentEqual.
Font load state is derived from the font faces associated with each shape.

assetUrls is supplied with keys whose values are undefined; those entries remain part of the optional mapping.

units.name: loadRequiredFontsForCurrentPage

detail.name: loadRequiredFontsForCurrentPage
preconditions: The editor dependency is initialized and can provide current-page shape IDs and shapes.
Each current-page shape ID resolves to a shape when passed to the editor.
postconditions: The font faces obtained from all current-page shapes are deduplicated by set membership.
If the number of unique required font faces is greater than limit, the asynchronous operation completes without continuing past the limit check.
invariants: Each font face is included at most once in the collected required-font set.
Only shapes returned by getCurrentPageShapeIds() are considered.
edgeCases: When the current page has no shapes, the collected required-font set is empty.
When multiple shapes require the same font face, that font face is counted once.
When the number of unique required fonts is greater than limit, the method returns early.
When limit is Infinity, the size-based early-return condition is not triggered by a finite required-font set.
detail.summary: Inspects the shapes on the current editor page and determines the unique font faces they require. If the number of required fonts exceeds the supplied limit, the method exits without continuing.

specLiterals.role: Default limit value indicating that finite required-font sets are not rejected by the size check.

specTests.when: loadRequiredFontsForCurrentPage is called with that limit.
specTests.then: Both shapes are inspected, the shared font face is counted once, and the operation does not take the over-limit early-return path.

units.name: ensureFontIsLoaded

detail.name: ensureFontIsLoaded
preconditions: font is a valid TLFontFace value.
The FontManager instance has access to its font-state store and editor document.
postconditions: If the font was already loading or ready, the existing loading promise is returned.
For a new request whose load succeeds, the loaded FontFace instance is added to the editor container document's fonts and the font state becomes ready.
For a new request whose load fails, the error is logged and the font state becomes error while the returned promise resolves.
If the request becomes stale because the font-state entry was replaced or cleared, the late completion does not modify the current font-state entry or document font set.
invariants: At most one loading promise is created per currently tracked font-state entry.
All completion handlers verify that the state entry is the exact entry created for the request before mutating state.
A rejected FontFace.load() is converted into a fulfilled Promise<void> after error handling.
edgeCases: When a state already exists for the font, no new FontFace is created or loaded; the existing loadingPromise is returned.
When FontFace.load() succeeds while the request is current, the instance is registered in the editor document and the state transitions from loading to ready.
When FontFace.load() rejects while the request is current, the rejection is logged and the state transitions from loading to error without propagating the rejection.
When dispose or another request makes the state entry stale before load completion, the completion is ignored for state and document mutation and the promise still resolves.

errorPolicy.returnsOnError: FontFace.load() errors are logged and the returned Promise<void> resolves after the font state is marked error; stale completion errors are debug-logged and otherwise ignored.

On successful current completion, adds the loaded FontFace instance to editor.getContainerDocument().fonts and updates the entry state to ready.
On failed current completion, updates the entry state to error.

detail.name: requestFonts
preconditions: fonts is an array of TLFontFace values.
postconditions: Every font supplied is added to the pending font set before the method returns.
A loading microtask is scheduled when no fonts were previously pending.
When the scheduled microtask runs for a non-disposed editor, the pending set is replaced with a new empty set and each distinct queued font is passed to ensureFontIsLoaded inside a transaction.
invariants: Pending fonts are deduplicated by Set identity.
Additional requests made while a batch is pending join the existing batch and do not schedule another microtask.
edgeCases: An empty fonts array still schedules a microtask when no fonts are pending; the resulting batch is empty.
Duplicate references in fonts are loaded at most once in the batch because pending fonts are stored in a Set.
If the editor is disposed before the queued microtask executes, the callback returns without loading fonts or clearing the pending set.
stateMutations: Adds supplied font face references to the private fontsToLoad Set.
For a non-disposed queued batch, replaces fontsToLoad with a new empty Set before invoking font loading.
detail.summary: Queues requested font faces for loading and batches requests received within the same microtask. Each distinct queued font is passed to the manager's loading routine unless the editor has been disposed before the batch executes.

specTests.when: requestFonts is called with two distinct font face references, followed by another call before the microtask runs.
specTests.then: Only one loading microtask is scheduled, and when it runs ensureFontIsLoaded is invoked once for each distinct requested font.
No font-loading calls occur and the pending font set is not cleared by that callback.

detail.name: findOrCreateFontFace
preconditions: font is a valid TLFontFace value.
this.editor provides a container Document with a FontFaceSet at document.fonts.
postconditions: Returns a FontFace matching the supplied family and default descriptor values.
The returned FontFace is cached for the container document and the font's cache key.
When a matching FontFace does not already exist, the newly created FontFace is added to the container document's FontFaceSet.
invariants: The cache is scoped per container Document, preventing reuse across documents or windows.
A cached FontFace is returned without scanning the document's FontFaceSet.
Existing matching FontFace instances are reused rather than duplicated.
Newly created FontFace instances use font display mode swap.

When the cache contains the font's key, the cached FontFace is returned immediately.
When the document already contains a matching family and all default descriptor values, that existing FontFace is cached and returned.
When the font source URL has no asset URL mapping, the original font source URL is used.
When the font source URL has an asset URL mapping, the mapped URL is used in the created FontFace.
When FontFace construction or adding the FontFace to the document fails, the error propagates to the caller.

detail.summary: Finds or creates a FontFace for the supplied font in the editor's container document. Repeated lookups for the same document and font descriptor reuse a cached or already-registered FontFace instead of creating duplicates.

specTests.when: findOrCreateFontFace is called again with that key.
specTests.then: The cached FontFace is returned without requiring another FontFaceSet scan or creating a duplicate.

units.name: toEmbeddedCssDeclaration
units.source:
const url = this.assetUrls?.[font.src.url] ?? font.src.url
		const dataUrl = await FileHelpers.urlToDataUrl(url)

		const src = compact([
			`url("${dataUrl}")`,
			font.src.format ? `format(${font.src.format})` : null,
			font.src.tech ? `tech(${font.src.tech})` : null,
		]).join(' ')
		return compact([
			`@font-face {`,
			`  font-family: "${font.family}";`,
			font.ascentOverride ? `  ascent-override: ${font.ascentOverride};` : null,
			font.descentOverride ? `  descent-override: ${font.descentOverride};` : null,
			font.stretch ? `  font-stretch: ${font.stretch};` : null,
			font.style ? `  font-style: ${font.style};` : null,
			font.weight ? `  font-weight: ${font.weight};` : null,
			font.featureSettings ? `  font-feature-settings: ${font.featureSettings};` : null,
			font.lineGapOverride ? `  line-gap-override: ${font.lineGapOverride};` : null,
			font.unicodeRange ? `  unicode-range: ${font.unicodeRange};` : null,
			`  src: ${src};`,
			`}`,
		]).join('\n')
	}
}

detail.name: toEmbeddedCssDeclaration
preconditions: font.src.url identifies a retrievable font resource.
FileHelpers.urlToDataUrl accepts the resolved source URL.
postconditions: The declaration uses a data URL for the font source.
Optional font descriptors are included only when their values are truthy.
The source format and technology hints are included when present.
invariants: The assetUrls mapping is preferred over the original font source URL when a mapping exists.
The generated declaration contains the font family and src descriptors.
Optional descriptors preserve their supplied values without transformation.
edgeCases: When assetUrls has no entry for font.src.url, the original font.src.url is passed to FileHelpers.urlToDataUrl.
When an assetUrls entry exists, that mapped URL is passed to FileHelpers.urlToDataUrl instead.
When format or tech is absent or falsy, its corresponding src descriptor is omitted.
When an optional font-face descriptor is absent or falsy, its CSS declaration line is omitted.
If URL-to-data-URL conversion fails, the resulting error propagates and no CSS declaration is returned.

errorPolicy.onInvalidInput: Not explicitly handled; invalid or unsupported input errors from URL conversion or subsequent processing propagate.

detail.ioFormatSpec: Returns a newline-separated CSS string in the form @font-face {, a quoted font-family declaration, zero or more optional descriptor declarations, a src declaration containing url("<dataUrl>") with optional format(...) and tech(...) hints, and }.
detail.summary: Converts a font source and its optional font-face descriptors into an embedded CSS @font-face declaration. The source URL is converted to a data URL before being included in the declaration.

specLiterals.role: Opening CSS font-face rule emitted by the method.
CSS source URL declaration format using the embedded data URL.
Closing CSS font-face rule emitted by the method.

specTests.then: It returns a CSS @font-face declaration containing font-family: "Inter";, src: url("data:font/woff2;base64,AAA") format(woff2);, and no absent optional descriptor lines.
The mapped asset URL is converted and the resulting data URL is used in the src declaration instead of the original URL.
The returned declaration includes each corresponding descriptor line and includes tech(<value>) in the src declaration.
